text: Found it: the proxy balancers panic when they have no targets — `randomBalancer.Next` indexes `b.targets[b.random.Intn(len(b.targets))]` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` computes `b.i % uint32(len(b.targets))`, both of which blow up (index out of range / divide by zero) on an empty target list. Fix: `Next` returns nil for an empty balancer, and the Proxy middleware returns 503 Service Unavailable instead of panicking. Applying and verifying now (~5 min).

`DefaultLoggerConfig.Output` is never actually set (it's nil), so the `if config.Output == nil { config.Output = DefaultLoggerConfig.Output }` defaulting at line 95-97 leaves it nil. At write time the code therefore takes the branch at lines 215-218 and writes the formatted log line to `c.Logger().Output()` — i.e. the `echo.Logger` of the Echo instance handling the request (which itself defaults to `os.Stdout`), not to `os.Stdout` directly. The doc comment on `Output` ("Default value os.Stdout") is only true because Echo's own default logger writes to os.Stdout.

Fixed and verified. In `middleware/proxy.go`:
- `randomBalancer.Next` now returns nil when `len(b.targets) == 0` (previously `b.targets[b.random.Intn(0)]` panicked).
- `roundRobinBalancer.Next` now takes the read lock and returns nil when there are no targets (previously `b.i % uint32(0)` → integer divide by zero panic).
- `ProxyWithConfig`'s handler now checks `if tgt == nil { return echo.ErrServiceUnavailable }` instead of dereferencing a nil target, so a balancer with no targets yields a clean 503.

Verification: `go build ./...` and `go vet ./middleware/` clean; `go test ./middleware/ -run TestProxy -v -count=1` and `go test ./... -count=1` fully green (baseline was also green, so no pre-existing test regressed); `-race` run of the proxy tests passes. A standalone repro confirmed the old code panics (`integer divide by zero` at proxy.go:188) and that with the fix both `NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{})` and `NewRandomBalancer(nil)` serve requests with HTTP 503 and `Next()` returns nil. No test files were modified.

It returns `echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, i.(error).Error())` — i.e. a 500 Internal Server Error whose message is the pooled value's error text (decompress.go lines 93-97). Note the code assumes the pool's non-`*gzip.Reader` value is an `error` and does an unchecked `i.(error)` assertion; that holds for `DefaultGzipDecompressPool`, whose `New` returns either a `*gzip.Reader` or an `error` from `gzip.NewWriterLevel`/`gzip.NewReader`, but a custom `Decompressor` returning some other type would panic there.
On it. Investigating `router.go`'s `Router.Find` for the non-routable-path case (panic / wrong match instead of a clean 404). I'll report again once I have the root cause and the fix verified.

`MethodOverride()` returns an `echo.MiddlewareFunc` — specifically `MethodOverrideWithConfig(DefaultMethodOverrideConfig)`. That middleware, on a `POST` request, reads the overridden method via the config's `Getter` (default `MethodFromHeader(echo.HeaderXHTTPMethodOverride)`, i.e. the `X-HTTP-Method-Override` header) and, if non-empty, replaces `req.Method` with it before calling the next handler; otherwise it just calls `next(c)`. Only `POST` can be overridden (method_override.go lines 37-39, 52-67).

#1 is fixed and verified: `middleware/proxy.go` — `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` now return nil for an empty target list (no more index-out-of-range / divide-by-zero panic), and `ProxyWithConfig` returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) when the balancer yields no target. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./middleware/`, `go test ./middleware/ -run TestProxy -count=1` and the full `go test ./... -count=1` are all green (baseline was green too, so no regression). No test files touched.

#4 (router.go / `TestRouterNoRoutablePath`) is still in progress: I'm reproducing which non-routable path cases panic or mis-match in `Router.Find`, then I'll apply the minimal fix and verify the whole test suite. ETA ~8 minutes.

It sets `config.Skipper = DefaultTrailingSlashConfig.Skipper` (redirect.go line 132) — note that's the *trailing-slash* middleware's default skipper, not `DefaultRedirectConfig.Skipper`. Both happen to be `DefaultSkipper`, so the behaviour is the same, but the reference is to the wrong config variable.

`limitedReader.Read` (middleware/body_limit.go lines 92-99) reads from the underlying reader, adds the bytes read to `r.read`, and if `r.read > r.limit` it returns `(n, echo.ErrStatusRequestEntityTooLarge)` — i.e. the number of bytes read in that call together with the 413 "Request Entity Too Large" error (not `io.EOF`). Otherwise it returns the underlying read result unchanged.

`DefaultBodyDumpConfig.Skipper` is `DefaultSkipper` (middleware/body_dump.go lines 34-39) — the shared no-op skipper from middleware/middleware.go, which always returns false, so nothing is skipped by default.

The `bytes_in` tag writes the `Content-Length` request header value, or the literal string `"0"` when that header is absent/empty: `cl := req.Header.Get(echo.HeaderContentLength); if cl == "" { cl = "0" }` (middleware/logger.go lines 187-192). So with no Content-Length header the log line contains `"bytes_in":0`.

`MethodFromQuery(param)` returns a `MethodOverrideGetter` — a `func(c echo.Context) string` that returns `c.QueryParam(param)`, i.e. the value of the given query-string parameter (method_override.go lines 86-92).

It sets `config.Skipper = DefaultGzipConfig.Skipper` (decompress.go line 77) — i.e. the *Gzip* middleware's default skipper rather than `DefaultDecompressConfig.Skipper`. Both are `DefaultSkipper` (always false), so behaviour is unchanged, but the reference points at the wrong config.

It panics: `panic(fmt.Errorf("echo: invalid body-limit=%s", config.Limit))` (body_limit.go lines 61-64), so an unparsable `Limit` (e.g. `BodyLimit("invalid")`) crashes at middleware-construction time rather than returning an error.
It panics with `"echo: body-dump middleware requires a handler function"` (body_dump.go lines 55-57) — the nil-handler check runs before the Skipper defaulting.

`http.StatusMovedPermanently` (301) — `DefaultRedirectConfig = RedirectConfig{Skipper: DefaultSkipper, Code: http.StatusMovedPermanently}` (redirect.go lines 27-30), and `redirect()` falls back to it when `config.Code == 0`.
#1 fixed and verified (proxy.go: empty balancer returns nil, middleware returns 503; full suite green).
#4 (router.go) still in progress — the reproduction/analysis subagent is still running; fix + verification ETA ~5 min.
#8 (context.go Scheme) in progress: `Scheme()` returns unvalidated forwarded-header values, so a bogus X-Forwarded-Proto leaks through; fix restricts them to "http"/"https". Verification ETA ~5 min.

#11 (bind.go) in progress: the map branch of `bindData` always does `reflect.ValueOf(v[0])`, which panics for `map[string][]string` (and on a nil map); fix handles slice element types and initialises nil maps. Verification ETA ~5 min.
#15 (group.go / TestMultipleGroupSamePathMiddleware) in progress: two groups with the same prefix must each keep their own middleware chain; a subagent is reproducing and fixing it. ETA ~5 min.
#18 (middleware/compress.go / TestGzipEmpty) in progress: empty responses must not keep `Content-Encoding: gzip` nor emit gzip bytes; a subagent is reproducing and fixing it. ETA ~5 min.

#8 fixed and verified. `context.go`'s `Scheme()` now only accepts a forwarded header value that is exactly "http" or "https" (X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Protocol, X-Url-Scheme); invalid values are ignored and fall through to the next check, finally returning "http". Precedence unchanged (TLS → X-Forwarded-Proto → X-Forwarded-Protocol → X-Forwarded-Ssl=="on" → X-Url-Scheme → "http"). `go build ./...`, `go vet ./`, `go test ./ -run TestContext` and the full `go test ./... -count=1` all pass; a scratch test covering the invalid-header cases passed and was deleted. No test files modified.

#11 fixed and verified. `bind.go`'s `bindData` map branch now initialises a nil map (`reflect.MakeMap`) and, when the map's element type is a slice, stores the whole `[]string` value instead of `v[0]` — so `map[string][]string` binds correctly instead of panicking with "reflect.Set: value of type string is not assignable to type []string", and a pointer-to-nil map no longer panics with "assignment to entry in nil map". `map[string]string` and the struct path behave as before. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./`, `go test ./ -count=1` and the full `go test ./... -count=1` all pass; a scratch test covering map[string][]string (incl. nil map), map[string]string, struct binding and end-to-end `c.Bind`/`BindQueryParams` passed and was deleted. No test files modified.
